text: If there would be a competition for the most naive men out there, then this subscriber of mine would probably get the first place. Imagine a situation. You have a girlfriend and she has a female friend. And the brother of that female friend is your girlfriend's ex. Now for some strange reason, your girlfriend likes to visit her female friend at her house. And not only visit, but to stay overnight, regularly. Would you be suspicious, or would you trust your girlfriend the same way my subscriber does? Let's go to the question to find out more. Hey man, I just want to say that I don't want my name to come out on this, but I need your opinion on something. That's another thing. I am not showing his name here, but I am wondering, who are you hiding from? If you are hiding from the people who are involved in the story, then wouldn't they guess who wrote the story by hearing it? But anyways, my girlfriend's ex is her very good friend's brother, so that means that whenever my girlfriend goes around her friend's house, which is a lot, she sees him there as well. I just feel uncomfortable with it, because when she has sleepovers there and stuff, it's just weird, because you are sleeping in the same house as your ex, and she goes to her friend's house a lot, so that means that she sees her ex a lot. Now she may not like him, but there is no way she just avoids him the whole time, as they used to be very close, and if you are in the same house, it is hard to avoid each other, especially as she goes to their house a lot. I also find it weird, because I remember her telling me that she once snuck out of her friend's room to go and see him back when they were dating, and that she used to stay up all night texting him, or just speaking to him without her friend knowing. So it just makes me think, surely those memories or feelings may come back, especially as she goes to the house a lot. Yeah, you said it many times already, man. I don't want to seem like an overthinker or weak, but I just need your help with what to do. It is just weird. Like, how do I know she isn't super friendly with him when she's at her friend's house, because she's super friendly to most people, even if she doesn't like them? And how do I know that she's not doing stuff that I wouldn't like when she's at her friend's house? It's just kind of odd, and I don't really like it, so if you could help me deal with this situation, that would be great. Thanks so much. Okay, so this was my answer. Hey man, damn, you might be one of the most naive men out there. If my girlfriend went to a house where her ex lives, let alone had a sleepover there, my ass would explode so hard, it could probably be seen from space. Now about that naivety. Do you seriously believe that your girlfriend goes to her friend's house, has sleepovers there, where her ex lives, and nothing happens? Between her and the man she slept with, kissed, did all sorts of things with, probably called the best, probably said she loved? Man, how naive can you be? The chances that something is going on between them are way more than 50%. Almost for sure there is emotional cheating, flirting, talking behind your back, some innocent conversations that are not so innocent. And very likely there is physical cheating too. If she genuinely wanted to see her female friend, she could pick hundreds of other options. Coffee, brunch, a walk, meeting in the city, but her house? With a sleepover? Come on man, that is not normal. Normally, in my advice, I say something like this. Talk to your girlfriend, explain how you feel, and if she understands your point and shows it through her actions, then maybe the relationship has a chance. But here? Man, run. You should have broken up yesterday. One more thing. You know how in a legal system there is a concept of presumption of innocence, where a person is innocent until proven guilty? In relationships, it works the other way around. Think of it as a presumption of guilt. Why? Because in a healthy relationship, the comfort of the other person is a priority. You should avoid doing things that could reasonably make your partner uncomfortable. And if you do something that looks suspicious, it is on you to clearly prove that nothing happened. Once again, your partner's comfort should come first. Anyway, I hope I was able to get my message across. What you do with it is up to you. So guys, don't be naive, write in the comments what do you think about this story. I hope it was informative and entertaining. My name is Ilyas Abdullin, thanks a lot and bye.
